subject: Auto-rollback on SLO breach: paging policy + oncall runbook updates
body:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Mar 4, 2025 at 9:12 AM PT
Subject: Auto-rollback on SLO breach: paging policy + oncall runbook updates

Rafael,

Can we align today on the paging policy for the new auto-rollback-on-SLO-breach integration before we wire incident-bot + oncall routing?

Two things I want to lock:
1) When do we page vs ticket for an automated rollback event?
2) What should the runbook say as the “first 10 minutes” workflow (verify monitors vs verify rollback executor vs broader incident)?

Drafts we’re iterating on:
- Runbook (DRAFT): https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/PLAT/Runbook%3A+Auto-rollback+on+SLO+breach+%28DRAFT%29
- Dashboard/alert spec (DRAFT): https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/PLAT/Rollout+SLO+dashboards+%26+alerting+spec+%28DRAFT%29
- SLO definitions (DRAFT): https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/SRE/SLO+definitions+for+rollouts+%28latency+%2B+error%29+%28DRAFT%29

My current proposal:
- Auto-rollback TRIGGERED (and succeeded): create ticket only (no page) unless it impacts >N tenants or occurs on “top routes” list.
- Auto-rollback TRIGGERED but rollback FAILED: page immediately (P1) to oncall.
- Monitor fetch/evaluator stuck/unknown verdict for >15m while rollout is in-progress: page (P2) since we lose safety net.

Let me know if you disagree. If we can get agreement today, Dylan can implement the incident-bot formatting and we can link the runbook directly from the alert.

— Sean
Sean Gallagher
Director, Site Reliability Engineering
Redwood Inference


From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Mar 4, 2025 at 10:03 AM PT
Subject: Re: Auto-rollback on SLO breach: paging policy + oncall runbook updates

Agree with most of this. I’d tweak a couple points to reduce noise/flapping:

1) “Rollback succeeded” should almost never page. Even if it’s a top route, the system behaved correctly. We should ticket + notify the owning team/channel, but paging on success trains oncall to ignore it.

2) For “unknown verdict” / monitor outage: I’d only page if (a) rollout is actively shifting traffic AND (b) we’re past warm-up window. Otherwise we’ll page on every planned canary when telemetry has a small delay.

3) For “multiple rollbacks”: paging threshold should be based on *rate* (e.g., >= 3 distinct tenants in 30 minutes) to catch global issues (capacity/region) without paging on a single customer’s bad config.

I can drop proposed exact thresholds into the runbook doc today. Also: runbook should explicitly call out the first step is validating whether the rollback was policy-driven vs manual override.

If you’re free, I can do 20 mins at 11:30.

— Rafael
Rafael Mendes
SRE Manager
Redwood Inference


From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Mar 4, 2025 at 10:18 AM PT
Subject: Re: Auto-rollback on SLO breach: paging policy + oncall runbook updates

+1 to Rafael’s point that “success” shouldn’t page.

From the tooling side, we can support three notification classes in incident-bot for this:
- INFO (Slack only): Auto-rollback succeeded
- WARNING (Slack + ticket): Auto-rollback succeeded but repeated (burst) OR rollback occurred on a protected route list
- PAGE: Rollback failed OR evaluator/monitor path broken during active rollout

We just need the decision table in the runbook + which labels to include in the message (tenant, route, region, model version, verdict window, baseline compare).

Also: can you confirm where you want the runbook link to land? I’d prefer a stable URL (non-draft) by GA.

— Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Console & Tooling
Redwood Inference


From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Mar 4, 2025 at 12:06 PM PT
Subject: Re: Auto-rollback on SLO breach: paging policy + oncall runbook updates

Good points.

Updates I’m comfortable with:
- No paging on rollback success.
- Ticket on success + Slack notify owning channel.
- Page conditions:
  A) rollback failed (executor error, config apply failure, idempotency conflict that leaves split unchanged)
  B) evaluator/monitor pipeline degraded while rollout is actively shifting traffic and past warm-up
  C) “burst rollbacks” indicating platform/region issue (rate-based threshold)

On the warm-up gating: let’s define it as “rollout in progress AND (traffic_to_candidate >= 10% OR rollout_age >= 15 min)” and only then page on unknown verdict.

Dylan: re stable URL, yes. We’ll publish Runbook: Auto-rollback on SLO breach under PLAT/runbooks once the content is locked; for now draft is fine.

Rafael: please do drop concrete thresholds into the runbook draft and tag me for final review.

Next: once we align, I’ll forward to Ava for awareness (we’ll want leadership to be aligned that we’re not paging on successful rollback events).

— Sean


From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Mar 4, 2025 at 2:22 PM PT
Subject: Fwd: Auto-rollback on SLO breach: paging policy + oncall runbook updates

Ava — quick heads up as we finalize GA readiness for auto-rollback-on-SLO-breach.

We’re aligning on a paging policy that avoids waking oncall when the automation succeeds. Summary:
- Auto-rollback succeeded: Slack notify + ticket only (for follow-up / regression tracking)
- Page only when (1) rollback fails, (2) evaluator/monitor path is broken during active rollout past warm-up (safety net missing), or (3) burst rollbacks suggest regional/platform incident

Draft runbook & alert spec:
- https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/PLAT/Runbook%3A+Auto-rollback+on+SLO+breach+%28DRAFT%29
- https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/PLAT/Rollout+SLO+dashboards+%26+alerting+spec+%28DRAFT%29

If you have concerns about the risk posture (esp. monitor outage behavior), please reply here. Otherwise we’ll proceed with this policy and implement incident-bot message classes accordingly.

— Sean

Subject: Re: Fwd: Auto-rollback on SLO breach: paging policy + oncall runbook updates

Aligned.

Strong preference that we do NOT page on “rollback succeeded” (agreed). If we see rollbacks spiking we can always tighten policies later, but early on we need signal > noise.

On monitor outage: paging only when actively shifting traffic + past warm-up is the right risk tradeoff.

Please make sure the runbook includes:
- what gets automatically created (ticket vs page)
- where to look in Console to confirm the split actually reverted
- how to pause/override if we suspect false positive

Thanks,
Ava

Redwood Inference


From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>, Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Mar 5, 2025 at 4:41 PM PT
Subject: Re: Auto-rollback on SLO breach: paging policy + oncall runbook updates

I updated the runbook draft with the decision table and thresholds.

Key additions:
- Notification policy table (INFO/WARNING/PAGE) with examples
- “Warm-up + low traffic” guardrails called out explicitly
- First 10 minutes checklist:
  1) Confirm candidate traffic % + whether rollback action applied (Console rollout page)
  2) Check evaluator verdict state (healthy/breaching/unknown) + reason
  3) Validate monitor freshness (dashboard panel + timestamp) before treating as a real regression
  4) If rollback failed: apply manual revert + open incident
- “Burst rollbacks” page threshold: >= 3 tenants in 30 minutes OR >= 2 regions affected in 30 minutes

Draft link (same): https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/PLAT/Runbook%3A+Auto-rollback+on+SLO+breach+%28DRAFT%29

If this looks good, Dylan can wire incident-bot with the same notification classes + include the runbook link.

— Rafael
